clue.text: Depressing way in which powerful people live

parts.note: depressing, as in pressing down, is downing
a street is a way or road

explanation.surface: A gloomy road where the mighty reside.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing Street in London is home to the Prime Minister and Chancellor of the Exchequer.
explanation.definitionFit: Downing Street houses Britain's Prime Minister and Chancellor, the country's most powerful politicians.

clue.text: Mean thing gored, maybe, by hungry cows

definitions.text: Mean thing gored, maybe, by hungry cows

indicators.note: maybe says the letters of these three words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A spiteful creature is perhaps tossed on the horns of starving cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: In Aesop's fable a dog lies in the hay it cannot eat and keeps the hungry oxen from it; the whole clue describes that spoiler, and its first three words are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a spiteful person who denies others something useless to himself, from the fable of the dog keeping cattle from their fodder.

clue.text: When errant airmen lose direction initially, some land in SE

indicators.note: initially asks for the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Lost aircrew going off course end up somewhere in south-east England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weald is a region of south-east England between the North and South Downs.
explanation.definitionFit: The Weald is a tract of once-wooded country across Kent, Sussex and Surrey in south-east England.

clue.text: Gen on reservations, etc, for those going singly ?

definitions.text: Gen on reservations, etc, for those going singly ?

parts.words: Gen on reservations, etc, for those going singly
parts.note: read as a dossier of information about the peoples living on American reservations, and also as the single-line marching order used by people walking one behind another

explanation.surface: Information about Native American reservations, for people who travel alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking in a single line, one behind another, was named after the way Native American war parties moved.

clue.text: It's hooked over ship's side by quiet angler somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: P, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quiet

explanation.surface: An angler quietly casts something over the side of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges P with ANGLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A grappling iron is a hooked tool thrown over a vessel's side to catch hold.

clue.text: In 1962 the latest innovation? Right

indicators.note: innovation, making something new, says the word latest is given a new order

explanation.surface: A quiz question: was this the newest thing in 1962? Correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Telstar, launched in 1962, was the first satellite to relay live television across the Atlantic; 'innovation' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telstar communications satellite was the newest marvel of 1962.

clue.text: Keeps encouraging, but surely that is that

definitions.meaning: to egg someone on is to urge them, so one who keeps urging does this
the saying 'as sure as ... is ...' means something is certain

explanation.walkthrough: The second part points to the idiom 'as sure as eggs is eggs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Egging on means urging, and the old phrase about eggs being eggs expresses certainty.

clue.text: Business with West Indies halved a blow

parts.note: trade is business or commerce

indicators.note: halved says only the first half of the word Indies is kept

explanation.surface: Commerce with the Caribbean was cut by half, a real setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'halved' cuts INDIES to IND.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade wind is a steady wind, and a blow is a gust or spell of wind.

clue.text: On your feet, buy a round-those are the rules

parts.note: someone on their feet is standing
buying a round of drinks means placing orders at the bar

explanation.surface: Get up and buy everyone a drink: that is the custom.
explanation.definitionFit: Standing orders are the permanent procedural regulations of a body such as Parliament.

clue.text: Fighter escort with flier-makes flight safer

parts.note: a guard is an escort, here protecting fighters
a rail is a bird, so a flier

explanation.surface: A warplane escort with another aircraft makes air travel safer.
explanation.walkthrough: The flight is a flight of stairs, not air travel.
explanation.definitionFit: A banister or handrail on a staircase stops people falling down a flight of steps.

clue.text: Gardener's job, producing palm-oil

definitions.meaning: ... a shoot onto a stock is a gardener's task
palm-oil is slang for bribery, money greasing a palm

explanation.definitionFit: Grafting is horticultural work, and graft is also corruption or bribery, which palm-oil denotes.

clue.text: North American can, when embracing her

indicators.note: the word can, embracing a girl, makes up the North American, so taking can away leaves her

parts.note: a Canadian is a North American

explanation.surface: A North American tin holds a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's tin is a red herring: 'can' is a word inside the nationality, and 'when embracing' says it wraps the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a woman's name, which a pronoun for a woman can stand for.

clue.text: Where bowlers aim to get catches ?

definitions.text: Where bowlers aim to get catches ?

parts.words: Where bowlers aim to get catches
parts.note: cricket practice areas enclosed in netting, where bowlers aim at batsmen and balls are caught, and also mesh things that catch fish

explanation.surface: Where cricket bowlers try to get batsmen caught out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the nets are netted practice lanes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket practice takes place in netted enclosures, and netting is also used to catch fish.

clue.text: Bird bit off another

indicators.note: off says the word bit is taken away from the other bird

parts.note: another bird here is the bittern, a heron-like marsh bird

explanation.surface: A bird pecked off part of a rival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another bird: take BIT off BITTERN.
explanation.definitionFit: A tern is a seabird related to the gulls.

clue.text: Tribe so mad, got into brief uprising

indicators.note: mad tells you to jumble the two letters of so
into says got is placed inside the other piece
uprising in a down clue turns the word for brief so it reads upwards

parts.note: brief means short

explanation.surface: Some tribesmen lost their minds and joined a short-lived revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' jumbles 'so'; in a down clue 'uprising' turns the brief word upwards, and 'into' puts 'got' inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ostrogoths were the eastern branch of the Goths, a Germanic people.

clue.text: Very nasty note, well within Trilby's capacity

indicators.note: well within says the note sits deep inside the other word

parts.note: a trilby is a hat, so its capacity is a hatful
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: An unpleasant musical note fits comfortably inside a hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A trilby is a soft felt hat with a dented crown.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hateful is odious, deserving loathing.

clue.text: Make out badly in tests, needing lessons"

indicators.note: in puts the scrambled word inside the tests

parts.note: trials are tests

indicators.note: badly says the letters of out are mangled

explanation.surface: Doing poorly in exams means you need extra teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' jumbles 'out' and 'in' places it inside the tests; 'Make' and 'needing' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutorials are teaching sessions given by a tutor to a small group.

clue.text: Composer in performance 19 gets across in it

indicators.note: in says the composer, placed inside the performance word, produces the clue's later words

parts.note: these clue words are what the composer becomes once the performance word wraps him; that he also sits as a run inside them is a coincidence of the construction
an act is a performance

explanation.surface: A musician on stage gets his message over to the audience.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual reverse-style clue: the composer placed inside the performance word yields the clue's last three words, so the composer is what remains when that word's three letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Metal transmuted to turn. into salt

indicators.note: transmuted, as an alchemist changes metals, says these letters are changed in order
turn says the little word to is turned around

explanation.surface: Alchemy turns metal into salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transmuted' rearranges METAL into MATEL, and 'turn' makes TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is slang for a sailor, as is an old salt.

clue.text: She's described as slovenly in writer's hearing.

indicators.note: in someone's hearing means spoken where they hear it, so the writer's name is said

parts.note: Anthony Trollope was the Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: A woman is called a slattern within earshot of an author.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist's name, said out loud, sounds like the slur.
explanation.definitionFit: A trollop is a slatternly or disreputable woman.

clue.text: Shot leads to Orient's game -hence grateful supporter

parts.note: shot as a verb means fired

indicators.note: leads to points to the leading letters of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A goal sends Orient's football team into a match, and a supporter is thankful.
explanation.walkthrough: Orient is a London football club. 'grateful' is read as grate-ful: an andiron supports logs in a grate.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog, or andiron, is a metal support holding logs in a fireplace grate.

clue.text: Has it a receptacle for ashes in front?

definitions.text: Has it a receptacle for ashes in front

indicators.note: in tells you the vessel goes inside the front

parts.note: a face is a front
an urn holds a cremated person's ashes

explanation.surface: A question about whether something has an ash-holder at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: A furnace's ash-pit is at its front, so the whole clue also describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A furnace is an enclosed fire chamber, which leaves ashes behind.

clue.text: Usual Somerville and Ross character's missing

parts.note: no, as in none present, means missing
Somerville and Ross wrote Some Experiences of an Irish R.M., about a Resident Magistrate

explanation.surface: A familiar figure from an Irish comic novel has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'character's missing' as 'the R.M. is missing', that is, no R.M.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the standard or usual pattern.

clue.text: Square boundary.

definitions.meaning: a square has this many sides
in cricket a ball reaching the boundary along the ground scores this many runs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a boundary is a shot reaching the edge of the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Four-sidedness defines a square, and a cricket boundary hit along the ground scores four runs.

clue.text: One relatively blessed in present circumstances

definitions.text: One relatively blessed in present circumstances

parts.words: One relatively blessed in present circumstances
parts.note: recalls the saying that it is more blessed to give than to receive, with present read as a gift

explanation.definitionFit: The biblical saying calls the donor of a gift more blessed than its recipient.

clue.text: One of Milton's harmonious sisters, say

definitions.meaning: in Milton's poem At a Solemn Music the 'sphere-born harmonious sisters' are ... and Verse
to say something is to utter or express it

explanation.definitionFit: Milton paired Voice with Verse as sister sirens, and to say is to utter or express.

clue.text: Adam in the garden, partly covering Eve's head

indicators.note: covering, in a down clue, puts the bed above the other letter

parts.note: a bed is one part of a garden

indicators.note: head points to the first letter of Eve's

explanation.surface: Adam in Eden partly hides Eve's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Adam Bede is George Eliot's novel and its hero, so Bede is Adam's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is the title character of George Eliot's first novel, named Adam.

clue.text: Wipe out HQ of Eritrean army secretly

annotationWithheld.why: Wipe out HQ of Eritrean army secretly (5): no sound parse found for ERASE; E from Eritrean is clear, but no reading of 'army secretly' gives RASE
annotationWithheld.clue: Wipe out HQ of Eritrean army secretly

clue.text: Extremely foolish, at any rate

definitions.meaning: the most foolish person is the one with the least wisdom
at any rate means at least, in any case

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means having the lowest wisdom; as one word it is a dialect form of at least.

clue.text: Top impressionists avoid it after retirement

definitions.text: Top impressionists avoid it after retirement

parts.words: Top impressionists avoid it after retirement
parts.note: read impressionists as people leaving an impression on the pillow and retirement as going to bed, so the best of them shun wakefulness at night

explanation.definitionFit: Insomnia, an inability to sleep after going to bed, is what good sleepers escape.
